reviewBoundary: Explicit new complete advanced and senior text practices, with objective keys and finite or bounded variants. Matching frozen originals supply level/task rules only. Author self-review covers whole-passage meaning, all candidate rationales and grammatical constraints; program checks do not imply independent teacher review, student calibration or production publication.

units.title: 高级词形：山间小屋的季节助理

materials.title: A Season at the Hut
materials.text:
The mountain hut advertised for two seasonal assistants. The work required physical ____1____ (FIT), but the manager warned applicants that strength alone was not enough. Guests arriving after a long walk could be tired, wet and unusually ____2____ (PATIENT). A calm reply was often more helpful than an energetic one.

The new assistants began with an ____3____ (INTRODUCE) to the building's water system. Water was stored in tanks, so daily use had to be recorded with reasonable ____4____ (ACCURATE). An impressive total written beside the wrong date would be of little practical value.

There was also a kitchen routine. Clear labels reduced the ____5____ (POSSIBLE) of confusing food intended for the evening meal with supplies kept for the following day. The manager welcomed suggestions, provided that a change was discussed before anyone put it into ____6____ (OPERATE).

By the end of the first month, the assistants understood why the job description had emphasised ____7____ (RELY). Being dependable meant completing small tasks even when nobody was watching. It also meant admitting a mistake promptly. The manager regarded that kind of ____8____ (HONEST) as a practical working skill, rather than merely a pleasant personal quality.

questions.explanation: physical后需表示体能的抽象名词fitness。
tired、wet与需要冷静回应共同支持不耐烦的impatient；题目要求与patient相反的形容词。
an后用名词introduction，指对供水系统的入门介绍。
with reasonable后需名词accuracy表示记录精确度。
the possibility of doing为可能性的名词结构。
put a change into operation表示实施改变，固定名词搭配。
下一句Being dependable解释可靠性reliability，reliance表示依赖而非个人可靠。
that kind of后需抽象名词honesty，回指主动承认错误。

units.title: 高级改写：遗憾、可能性与请人修理

materials.title: Six Precise Changes
materials.text:
Complete each second sentence so that it keeps the meaning of the first. Use three to six words, including the given word unchanged. Do not change the words outside the gap.

1. I regret not allowing more time for the test. (WISH)
I ____1____ more time for the test.

2. They will probably publish the report next week. (LIKELY)
The report ____2____ next week.

3. She was very nervous, but she answered the question confidently. (HOWEVER)
____3____, she answered the question confidently.

4. The severe weather was the only reason they did not go on the trip. (BUT)
____4____, they would have gone on the trip.

5. The piano is too large to fit through the door because the doorway is too narrow. (ENOUGH)
The door ____5____ the piano.

6. Rosa arranged for a specialist to repair her telescope last month. (HAD)
Rosa ____6____ last month.

questions.explanation: 对已发生的未留足时间表示遗憾，wish后用过去完成had allowed。
report是被发表对象，be likely to后接被动to be published。
however +形容词+主语+系动词引导让步，保持虽紧张但自信作答的意义。
But for +名词短语表示要不是，完整五词短语填入空内，符合三至六词边界并保留BUT；Because of不能构成同样的过去虚拟条件。
门不够宽容纳钢琴，enough置于形容词wide之后；允许is not/isn't两个常用形式。
have+物+过去分词表示让别人修理，不能改成Rosa本人完成修理；上下文只有该望远镜，her/the均可指回。

units.instruction: Preserve the meaning and use the given word unchanged; obey the word range shown for each item.

units.title: 高一完形：黎明步行时听见的间隔

materials.title: Before the Street Woke
materials.text:
On the morning of the town's dawn walk, I nearly stayed in bed. The notice had promised a chance to hear birds before the streets became ____1____. My father had signed us up, but I could see little reason to get dressed before the sun was even ____2____.

At the meeting place, the guide asked us to stand still for a minute. I expected a ____3____ chorus. Instead, I heard a distant engine and the soft movement of coats. “There is nothing here,” I whispered. The guide did not ____4____ with me. She pointed towards the hedge and lifted one finger, asking us to wait.

A short, clear call came from inside the leaves. Another followed from the opposite side of the path. The guide asked whether the two sounds were ____5____. I had been listening for loudness, not pattern, and could not answer. On the next calls, I noticed that one ended sharply while the other seemed to ____6____ away.

We walked slowly to the river. Whenever somebody heard a new sound, the group stopped. I began to notice the ____7____ between calls as well as the calls themselves. Once, I raised my hand at the sound of a gate, and several people smiled. The guide explained what had made the noise without making me feel ____8____.

By the time we returned, my father had taken only one photograph: a muddy pair of boots beside a puddle. I had nothing impressive to ____9____ my friends on a screen. Yet I found myself stopping in our street to listen to a bird I had previously ____10____.

At breakfast, I tried to describe the walk. My first sentence was, “It was quiet.” Then I ____11____ myself. There had been plenty to hear; I had simply expected everything to arrive at once. The calls were no ____12____ than before; I was listening differently. The guide had changed the way I gave them my ____13____.

The next weekend, I set an alarm without being asked. I did not expect the same calls or the same weather. That ____14____ was part of the attraction. I wanted to find out what the morning would ____15____ this time.

questions.explanation: B正确：黎明先听鸟，赶在人车街道繁忙前。A空旷不是黎明后要避开的噪声状态；C宽窄不随时段变；D是否笔直无关。
D正确：before dawn太阳尚不可见，解释为何起床早。B熟悉与否不表示天亮；C有用和A舒服不是此处太阳出现的时间状态。
C正确：作者期待鸟鸣突然齐响，与实际需细听一两声相对。A无声合唱与期待听鸟相矛盾；B破碎未能表达预期热闹；D私密不表示声响。
A正确：向导没有争辩“这里什么都没有”，而用手势等待事实。C与作者旅行已发生，不合with me此处回应；D分享缺少宾语；B没有比赛。
C正确：下一句比较两声结尾模式，问是否相似。D声音重量不合；A现代性未讨论；B没有安全判断。
B正确：一个声尾尖短，另一个渐弱消退，fade away固定表达。D跳、A转和C断均不表达逐渐变弱。
D正确：作者开始关注鸟叫之间的间隔。A图像不是声音间的东西；C指令未在每次叫声间出现；B阴影不是本段听觉关注点。
A正确：误把门声当新鸟声，向导解释而不使作者难堪。C受欢迎与避免尴尬相反维度；B饥饿无关；D不让人感到受欢迎不是此友善情境。
C正确：没有可在屏幕上展示给朋友的精彩照片。B借屏幕内容不是这里的交流；D未借需还物品；A承诺不需屏幕。
B正确：以前忽略的街边鸟现在引起注意。C未描述曾保护；A未跟踪；D没有曾命名的线索。
D正确：他说安静后立刻修正，因为其实可听声音很多。A不是介绍自己；B自娱非更正说法；C保暖与话语无关。
A正确：no ... than要求比较级，louder呼应此前只关注音量。B是副词原级；C是名词；D是副词而非形容词比较级，都不能填入calls were no ... than结构。
C正确：give attention to表示将注意力给予鸟声。D不需要人许可才鸣叫；B距离不能“给予”鸟；A方向不合搭配。
D正确：不预期相同鸟声天气，未知变化本身吸引人。A固定日程不包含变化；B作者并不失望；C不保证安静。
B正确：find out what the morning would bring表示期待早晨带来的新经历。A：carry侧重承载，不构成此处期待经历的惯用表达；C：keep表示保留而非带来新经历；D：follow表示跟随，不合早晨带来体验的语义。

units.title: 高一阅读：果园周末与一块丝线样布

materials.title: An Orchard Weekend
materials.text:
The orchard at Meadow Farm opens for two different activities in September. On Saturday mornings, visitors can join a guided walk to learn how apples are picked and stored. The walk lasts ninety minutes and stays on the firm path between the trees. Picking fruit is not included, but participants can taste three varieties at the packing shed afterwards.

Sunday afternoons are for apple picking. Visitors collect a basket at the entrance and pay for the weight of fruit they take home. The farm asks people to use only the rows marked with yellow signs. Apples in other rows may not be ready, even when their skins look equally red. Staff demonstrate how to lift and turn a fruit gently, leaving its short stem attached. Ladders are not available, so visitors should choose apples they can reach while standing on the ground.

Both activities require booking. A guided-walk ticket cannot be used for Sunday picking, because the farm limits the number of people in the orchard differently on the two days. Families who want to do both must make separate reservations. If heavy rain closes the picking rows, visitors are offered another Sunday or a refund; the farm shop may remain open, but a shop visit does not replace the picking activity.

A small display in the shed explains the orchard's storage system. Some apples are sold soon after harvest, while others are kept for later months. The farm does not label every red apple as suitable for long storage. Variety and condition matter as well as colour. Visitors who want advice for fruit from their own gardens can bring a photograph and a written description to the Saturday walk. Staff cannot identify every variety from a photograph, but may suggest what to check next.

questions.prompt: What is included in the Saturday guided walk?
options: Taking home a basket of apples at no cost.
Tasting several varieties after the walk.
Using ladders to reach high fruit.
Picking from any row without signs.
questions.explanation: B正确：周六走后可在包装棚尝三种苹果。A未含免费带走篮果；C不提供梯子；D周六不含采摘，周日也限黄标行。

questions.prompt: Why are Sunday visitors restricted to yellow-signed rows?
options: The other rows contain no apple trees.
All fruit outside them is kept only for photographs.
Fruit in the other rows may not yet be ready to pick.
The signs show which apples have the reddest skins.
questions.explanation: C正确：其他行果实即使同样红也可能未成熟。A没有说别行无树；B不是摄影专用果；D黄标判成熟区而非皮色最红。

questions.prompt: What should a family do if it wants both activities?
options: Book the walk and picking separately.
Use one Saturday ticket for both days.
Wait until the shop replaces a closed picking session.
Pay for the guided walk according to the fruit’s weight.
questions.explanation: A正确：两天按不同人数限制，必须分别预订。B票不能通用；C商店访问不替代采摘；D按果重付费只用于周日采摘果。

materials.title: A Small Piece of Silk
materials.text:
When Hana started learning embroidery, she wanted to make a complete picture as quickly as possible. Her teacher gave her a square of plain cloth and asked her to work six different lines across it. Hana thought the exercise looked dull. There was no bird, flower or finished scene to show her family.

The first line used a simple running stitch. The second required the thread to pass around earlier stitches. Hana pulled it tightly to make the line look neat, but the cloth began to gather into folds. The teacher did not remove the work. She asked Hana to leave half the line as it was and continue the other half with a looser tension. The two sections became a useful comparison that Hana could feel with her fingers.

Over the following weeks, the square filled with short lines, curves and patches. Hana wrote the thread type and needle size beside each new section on a paper chart. Sometimes a method that worked well with fine silk felt awkward with thick wool. The chart helped her remember which combination she had actually tried rather than which one she thought she remembered.

Several months later, Hana began a picture of a harbour. Before filling the water, she tested three ways of making a soft reflection on a spare corner of the practice cloth. She chose one and kept the other samples too. The original square never became a finished decorative picture. It remained beside her sewing basket, increasingly worn but still useful. When a visitor asked why she kept an untidy piece of cloth, Hana could point to particular marks that had saved her from repeating a difficulty in a larger work.

questions.prompt: What initially disappointed Hana about the practice task?
options: It had no complete decorative scene.
It required her to use a sewing machine.
It involved making clothes for strangers.
It had to be finished without any teacher.
questions.explanation: A正确：她想做鸟花等成图，而练习只有不同线条。B是手工针线，没有机器要求；C没有给陌生人做衣；D老师一直指导。

questions.prompt: Why was part of the tightly sewn line left unchanged?
options: So the folds could be hidden under a finished picture.
So Hana could compare it with a more loosely worked section.
Because the teacher thought tight stitches always worked best.
Because the cloth could not hold any more thread.
questions.explanation: B正确：保留一半并放松另一半，形成可触摸的张力对比。A没有遮盖折痕；C紧拉导致起皱，并非总最好；D后来继续加线和样块。

questions.prompt: What made the old cloth useful when Hana began the harbour picture?
options: It supplied a compulsory pattern that everyone had to copy.
It proved that wool and silk behaved in exactly the same way.
It let her test and remember methods before using them in larger work.
It had become more valuable as a decorative object than the harbour picture.
questions.explanation: C正确：样布可试反光针法、保留失败和材料记录，避免在大作中重犯困难。A不是强制模板；B不同材料感受不同；D她保留的是实用价值，未比较价格。

units.title: 高二完形：从岸边到船上的池塘地图

materials.title: Turning the Paper
materials.text:
For our geography project, we had to draw a map of a place we knew well. Most classmates chose a shopping street or a sports centre. I chose the small pond where my uncle kept his rowing boat. I thought it would be ____1____, because I had visited it many times.

From the bank, I drew an island, a low bridge and a row of tall trees. Then my uncle suggested that we check the map from the boat. As soon as we moved away from the bank, my familiar landmarks looked ____2____. The trees hid part of the bridge, and the island seemed closer to the far shore than I remembered.

I turned the paper several times, trying to make it ____3____ the view. My uncle waited while I worked out which end of the map should point towards the bridge. He did not simply take the pencil and ____4____ it for me. When I finally lined up two clear landmarks, the other features began to make sense.

There was still a problem. I had drawn the island much ____5____ than the space between it and the bank. We rowed slowly along that stretch while I counted regular strokes. I knew this was not an exact way of measuring distance, but it gave me a better sense of ____6____. Back on the bank, I changed the drawing instead of keeping the neat first version.

At school, a friend asked why my map included the words “view from the south bank”. I explained that my first sketch had recorded how the pond looked from one ____7____. The final map tried to show where things were in relation to one another. Naming the starting position helped explain the ____8____ between those two kinds of picture.

My teacher did not expect a professional survey. She asked me to describe how I had checked my choices. I could point to the turned paper, the partly hidden bridge and the distance I had ____9____. The map was not as tidy as the one I had first imagined, but its changes made the ____10____ behind it visible.

When I returned to the pond later, I brought a clean copy for my uncle. He ____11____ it beside the boat shed. I thought this meant he believed it was perfect. Then he gave me a pencil and asked what I might add if the fallen tree near the island was ____12____ before spring. I saw that a map could be finished enough to use without being finished for ____13____. I wrote the month in a corner and left a little space for ____14____. This time, an empty part of the paper felt like an ____15____ rather than a failure.

questions.explanation: B正确：经常去池塘让作者起初觉得画图容易。A学校作业非官方测绘；C地点不保密；D未说费用。
D正确：角度改变使地标遮挡和相对位置看起来不同。B并非都变小；C仍有岛桥树；A没有危险事件。
C正确：旋转纸让地图方向与眼前景色匹配。A盖住景色非目的；B不是回避观察；D景色不能借用。
A正确：叔叔不替他直接改正定位，而让其自己想明白。C没有藏图；D不是售卖；B折纸不解决地标关系。
C正确：岛与岸间距比例失真，画的岛宽过实际相对距离；后文重新感受尺度。D声音、A清洁、B亮暗均不是图上比例问题。
B正确：数划桨大致估距，改善图中尺度比例。D不测天气；A地图朝向已靠地标对齐解决；C数次数非比赛速度。
D正确：第一稿记从一个观察位置所见。A特定季节不是前后视图差异；C位置不是答案；B只凭回忆与最初实地岸边写生不符。
A正确：命名起点便于解释视角图与相对位置地图的区别。C两类图不称协议；B有联系但后句强调各自所表现内容不同；D不是两张纸之间的物理距离。
C正确：他用数桨重新考虑并修改先前的距离。B他实际核查并未忽略；D距离无隐藏；A没作距离承诺。
B正确：保留修改使决策思考过程可见。C没有售价；A没比赛；D没有许可申请。
D正确：固定在船棚旁让地图可用，作者以为这是认可。A扔掉、B掉下、C焚毁都不支持认可和后续询问。
A正确：倒树移走会改变地标，需更新图。B涂色、D计数、C拍照不导致地图中地标不复存在。
C正确：finished for ever表示永远完成，与现在够用、将来仍需更新相对。A：for once表示难得一次，不能表达永久不变；B：for sale表示待售，文章并非卖图；D：for nothing表示徒劳，不合当前地图已可使用的事实。
D正确：标月并留空，便于未来更新。A不需要签名；B不为奖品；C不是主动给错误留位置。
B正确：留空被视为邀请将来修订而非失败。A不是偶然损伤；D不是命令；C不是推卸责任。

units.title: 高二阅读：冬日树芽与放映室的接片台

materials.title: What the Bare Branches Held
materials.text:
In winter, the orchard beside Halden School seemed empty to many pupils. They could see no leaves, and the apples had long been collected. Their science teacher, Priya Sen, used this apparent emptiness as the starting point for a short observation project. She asked each pair to choose one low branch and draw what they could actually see, without adding a leaf from memory.

At first, several drawings showed little more than a line. Looking again through a hand lens, the pupils noticed small buds along the twigs. Priya explained that a bud was not simply a mark on the bark. It protected developing structures that would become active later. She avoided promising that every bud would produce a flower. Some would produce leaves, and some might be damaged before spring.

The pupils tied loose paper labels near their chosen branches so that they could return to the same places. Their next drawings included the buds' positions and shapes. One pair chose two different branches on the same tree. This allowed them to compare a specific bud with itself over time, while also noticing that neighbouring buds did not always change on the same day.

As warmer weather arrived, the project became harder rather than easier. Small changes happened between visits, and a bird removed one of the labels. The pair whose label disappeared used their earlier drawing of the branch fork to locate the original twig. Their drawing had become more than a record of appearance: it also held the information needed to repeat an observation.

At the end of term, the class displayed sequences of drawings rather than selecting only the neatest final picture. A visitor could follow which features had appeared, moved or been lost. The winter pages were no longer treated as incomplete pictures awaiting leaves. They showed the starting conditions that made the later changes understandable.

questions.prompt: Why did Priya ask pupils not to add leaves from memory?
options: She wanted drawings based on the branch’s current observable features.
She believed leaves had never grown in the orchard.
She wanted to replace observation with an art competition.
She expected every winter bud to become a flower.
questions.explanation: A正确：要求记录当下实际所见，而非凭记忆添加不存在的叶子。B果园过去有叶并未被否认；C没有比赛；D她明确避免保证所有芽开花。

questions.prompt: How did one drawing help after a paper label was lost?
options: It identified the bird that had taken the label.
It supplied a new name for the tree.
It showed the branch fork needed to find the original twig.
It proved that all nearby buds changed at once.
questions.explanation: C正确：学生凭早期图中的分叉定位原枝。A没查明是哪只鸟；B无需新树名；D邻芽变化日期未必相同。

questions.prompt: What did displaying sequences of drawings make possible?
options: Hiding the winter stages of the project.
Understanding later changes in relation to their starting conditions.
Choosing the most attractive tree without studying it.
Guaranteeing that no label would ever be lost.
questions.explanation: B正确：序列展示让读者把新特征与最初状态对应。A冬页被保留；C不是选最漂亮的树；D展图不能保证标签永不丢。

materials.title: The Joining Table
materials.text:
Before films were stored as digital files at the Regent Cinema, projectionists worked with long strips of film. Leila Marr began there as an assistant when she was nineteen. She expected the most important place to be beside the projector's bright beam. Her first lessons, however, took place at a small table in a separate room.

An experienced colleague showed her how to inspect a film strip for damage and join two ends accurately. A join that looked acceptable while lying on the table could fail when the strip moved through the projector. Leila practised with discarded material, then ran it through a hand-operated viewer. She learned to feel a raised edge with her finger before she could always see it.

The work was neither completely mechanical nor purely a matter of personal judgement. There were clear procedures, but different kinds of wear required attention. Leila kept brief notes about recurring problems and asked colleagues to explain repairs she had not encountered. She also learned when a damaged section should be referred to somebody with more experience rather than repaired in a hurry.

Years later, the cinema changed to digital projection. Leila had new systems to learn, and the joining table was no longer part of the daily programme. When the building held an anniversary open day, she brought it out of storage and demonstrated the old process using unwanted film. Visitors were surprised that so much work had happened away from the beam they remembered seeing.

Leila did not describe the earlier system as better in every respect. A worn join could interrupt a screening, and handling film took time and space. What she wanted visitors to notice was a kind of preparation that had usually remained invisible. The table helped her explain how a seemingly continuous experience in the auditorium had depended on many carefully made connections elsewhere.

questions.prompt: What did Leila discover at the start of her training?
options: Preparation away from the projector required important practical skills.
All damaged film could be repaired without training.
The joining table was only a decorative object.
Working near the projector’s beam was the only task worth learning.
questions.explanation: A正确：她先在另一房间学检查接片，发现重要工作不都在光束旁。B有些需请更有经验者处理；C接片台承担日常技术任务；D与其最初受训内容相反。

questions.prompt: Why did Leila test joins in a hand-operated viewer?
options: To turn old film into digital files.
To check how a join behaved when the strip moved.
To remove the need for any written procedure.
To make every repair invisible to her colleagues.
questions.explanation: B正确：静放看着好也可能运动时失败，因此模拟运行检查。A不是数字转换；C仍有清楚程序；D目的不是对同事隐瞒。

questions.prompt: What was Leila’s purpose in demonstrating the old table?
options: To prove digital projection could never produce a continuous screening.
To ask the cinema to return permanently to old equipment.
To show only the most dangerous part of the former job.
To make normally hidden preparation understandable to visitors.
questions.explanation: D正确：她希望观众理解银幕连续体验背后的接片准备。A未否定数字放映；B未要求永久换回；C不是突出危险，且说明旧制也有缺点。

units.title: 高三完形：餐馆最后一晚的普通水壶

materials.title: Flowers in a Water Jug
materials.text:
On the last evening before my aunt closed her little restaurant, I arrived with a camera. I wanted to record every ____1____ before the room changed. For thirty years, she had served lunches there, and I thought the final service deserved a set of perfect pictures.

I began with the empty tables. My aunt asked me to move a chair, and I waited until she had finished ____2____ the scene. “It is not a scene,” she said. “I need that space to carry the soup.” I put down the camera and helped her ____3____ a path between the tables.

The first customer was a man who usually came alone and read beside the window. That evening he brought a small bunch of flowers. My aunt found an ordinary water jug because the tall vase would have ____4____ his view. I almost asked them to pose, but the man had already opened his book. The moment seemed more valuable if I did not ____5____ it.

Later, a family arrived with a child who had once been frightened by the kitchen bell. She now insisted on ringing it herself. My aunt ____6____ her up so that she could reach, then handed her the first bowl of rice. Nothing about the action was arranged for my lens.

Between orders, I noticed the notebook beside the till. It contained no elegant recipes. There were lists of suppliers, birthdays and meals that regular customers could not ____7____ because of food allergies. I had photographed the painted menu outside, but this small book revealed a different kind of ____8____: the details my aunt kept in order to look after particular people.

When the last guests left, I asked her to stand in the doorway. She agreed, on the ____9____ that I would take only one picture before helping with the washing-up. In the photograph, one sleeve was wet, and a tea towel hung from her ____10____. I first regarded these details as things to edit away.

Now I leave them in. They remind me that the restaurant was a place of work as well as a setting for my ____11____. The final evening did not become important because I had ____12____ it carefully. Its importance was already there, in the small exchanges I had nearly interrupted.

My aunt keeps the doorway photograph in her new kitchen. I keep several others, including one of the window table after the reader had gone. His flowers are still in the water jug. It is not the most ____13____ arrangement in the collection, but I can remember why it was made that way. That ____14____ gives the image a place in the story. Without it, the jug would be just another object I had ____15____ before the room was cleared.

questions.explanation: B正确：作者要在房间改变前记录每个细节，符合拿相机拍完美照片。A没有每条投诉；C镜头不直接记录利润；D不是旅行记录。
D正确：作者以为姑妈在摆好拍摄场景，下一句纠正只是要运汤通道。B不需等想象完成才拍；C姑妈并未离开房间；A不是研究场景。
C正确：移椅子清出端汤通道。A没测量；B堵住与运输相反；D不是隐藏通道。
A正确：高花瓶会挡住窗边视线，改用普通水壶。C若改善视野则不用改；D没有反射功能；B不是保护视线免受什么伤害。
C正确：读者已看书，作者放弃摆拍不打断自然时刻。D识别、A记住、B描述均不会强制改变当时行为。
B正确：把孩子抱高让她够到铃。D跟随不能提高身高；A推搡不符照顾情境；C转身不保证够到。
D正确：为顾客照顾饮食限制，记录不能吃的餐食。A不会做饭不等于餐馆需避开的饭菜；C不能点餐无原因；B看不见与饮食记忆无关。
A正确：笔记体现对具体顾客细节的关注。C雄心不由生日忌口体现；B不是教学指令；D没有竞争活动。
C正确：on the condition that为以……为条件，只拍一张就洗碗。B证据、D希望、A怀疑不合固定条件表达。
B正确：茶巾自然从手上垂下，显示仍在工作。C天花板不属于her；A姑妈不是持相机拍自己的人；D照片内部物不能从照片表面悬挂。
D正确：对作者来说餐馆承载往事，但姑妈还在这里工作。A他不是为推广新营业拍广告；B无操作指令；C没有投诉动机。
A正确：作者认识到价值不是因自己认真拍摄才产生。B并未装修；D当晚是关门前最后营业非重开；C没有替换餐馆。
C正确：普通水壶插花不最优雅，但有为顾客保留视线的原因。D布置谈不上准确量值；B价格未被强调；A花朵也非永久物件。
D正确：知道为何这样摆放提供语境，使照片进入故事。A表面、B距离、C安静均不包含摆放理由。
B正确：相机capture物件影像，房间清空前拍下。A没有修水壶；D没有借走物件；C水壶真实存在非杜撰。

units.title: 高三阅读：球场预约与绳结的数学问题

materials.title: Who Appeared in the Booking List?
materials.text:
The recreation department in Linton wanted to find out whether residents would use additional tennis courts. It sent a questionnaire to everyone who had booked one of the existing courts during the previous year. Many respondents said they would welcome more evening sessions. The department's first summary therefore described strong demand for additional courts across the town.

A community organiser questioned that wording. The responses were useful, she said, but the booking list contained only people who had already overcome the practical barriers to making a reservation. Residents without a suitable partner, people unable to use the online system and those put off by the current fees might never appear on it. Their absence did not establish that they disliked tennis. Nor did it prove that they wanted new courts. It meant that the questionnaire had not yet asked them.

The department then arranged short conversations at the public library, a youth centre and a weekend market. These were not a perfect substitute for a carefully designed town-wide sample. People passing those places had their own characteristics. Nevertheless, the conversations exposed a possibility that the original questionnaire had barely addressed: some residents were more interested in beginner sessions with equipment provided than in extra bookable court hours.

The revised proposal separated two decisions. One was whether existing users needed more evening capacity. The other was whether a different kind of programme could enable new participants to try the sport. Officials kept the questionnaire results as evidence for the first decision while running a small, separately assessed beginner programme for the second. They withdrew the claim that a single booking-list survey represented the whole town. The additional work did not make the first answers worthless; it made the population to which those answers applied more precise.

questions.prompt: What was the main weakness in the department’s first summary?
options: It counted each completed questionnaire as a formal court reservation.
It generalised answers from previous bookers to residents across the town.
It assumed that all existing courts were empty in the evening.
It stated that none of the respondents wanted additional sessions.
questions.explanation: B正确：只问旧预约者，却把需求表述为全镇，外推范围过大。A问卷不是预约；C恰有晚间加场需求；D多数回答欢迎更多晚场。

questions.prompt: What did the organiser say about people absent from the booking list?
options: Their preferences had not been established by the questionnaire.
They had all rejected tennis after trying it.
They were certain to prefer new courts to beginner lessons.
Their absence proved that current fees were affordable.
questions.explanation: A正确：没被问到不等于不喜欢或一定想新球场。B与C都是未经询问的断言；D费用可能正是障碍。

questions.prompt: How did the revised proposal use the original questionnaire?
options: It treated the responses as a complete measure of new participants’ needs.
It removed every existing user from future planning.
It kept the responses for a more narrowly defined capacity question.
It replaced all evidence with an assumption about equipment costs.
questions.explanation: C正确：保留旧用户晚场容量证据，另测新入门项目。A再次过度推及新人；B没有排除老用户；D也没有放弃证据。

materials.title: A Different Question about a Knot
materials.text:
At the beginning of a mathematics workshop, the tutor gave each participant a closed loop of soft cord. She asked them to form a loose shape on the table, then move the cord without cutting it or allowing one section to pass through another. The question was not how attractive a pattern they could make. It was whether two very different-looking arrangements could still be regarded as the same kind of object under those rules.

Some participants initially measured the distances between points on the table and the angles between nearby sections of cord. The tutor explained that these quantities could change as the cord was moved, so they could not by themselves settle the question. A narrow loop could become a broad one without being cut. A crossing in a drawing could also be misleading: it might show one section passing above another, rather than the cord physically going through itself.

The participants worked in pairs. One person rearranged the cord while the other recorded which moves had been made. When a pair believed that two shapes were equivalent, they demonstrated a sequence of permitted moves. Showing such a sequence provided a clear argument for that case. Failing to find a sequence, however, did not automatically prove that none existed. The tutor asked them to keep those two kinds of statement separate.

Later, the class discussed the need for features that would remain unchanged under every permitted move. If two arrangements differed in such a feature, that difference could rule out their equivalence. The workshop did not turn everyone into an expert in knot theory, and some proposed features failed when another pair found a counterexample. What it offered was a change in the kind of question being asked. Instead of describing how a shape looked at one moment, the participants began asking what could or could not change while a rule-governed process continued.

questions.prompt: Why could those distances and angles not settle the workshop’s central question?
options: The rules required the cord to remain straight at all times.
Participants were forbidden to look closely at their loops.
Those measurements could change during permitted movements.
All loops had been cut into separate pieces before the task.
questions.explanation: C正确：移动中长度形态和角度可变化，不能单独决定规则下的等价。A规则允许变形；B可以近看操作；D全程不允许切开。

questions.prompt: What did demonstrating a permitted sequence establish?
options: That the two arrangements in that case could be connected under the rules.
That every possible arrangement was equivalent to every other one.
That a failed search could prove no sequence existed.
That drawings could never represent a physical cord.
questions.explanation: A正确：展示合法步骤证明这一对能互转。B不推广到所有对象；C寻找失败不证明不存在；D绘图只是可能误导交叉，不是永不能用。

questions.prompt: What kind of feature could help rule out equivalence?
options: One selected only because it made a pattern attractive.
An angle measured before anyone moved the cord.
A feature that changed whenever a drawing was rotated.
One preserved by all permitted moves but different between the arrangements.
questions.explanation: D正确：若合法移动全保持某特征而两构型该特征不同，就不能等价。A美感不是规则量；B角度可改变；C旋转即变的量不是所需不变量。
